claims.text: Pericarditis: colchicine (eg, 0.5 or 0.6 mg once or twice daily) with aspirin or another NSAID;
claims.quote: usually in combination with colchicine (eg, 0.5 or 0.6 mg once or twice daily)

claims.text: 3 months as an adjunct significantly cuts recurrence and symptom persistence after a first episode.
claims.quote: Colchicine for 3 months as an adjunct significantly decreases the recurrence rate and symptom persistence in patients with a first episode of acute pericarditis

claims.text: Painful recurrences may respond to NSAIDs and/or twice-daily colchicine for 6–12 months with a gradual taper.
claims.quote: Painful recurrences of acute pericarditis may respond to NSAIDs and/or twice daily colchicine for 6 to 12 months with a gradual taper.
